facts.claim: 22/24 lineages of Escherichia coli and Pseudomonas fluorescens independently evolved heritable mechanisms of resistance to pexiganan when propagated in medium supplemented with this antimicrobial peptide for 600-700 generations.
facts.quote: In this selection experiment, 22/24 lineages of Escherichia coli and Pseudomonas fluorescens independently evolved heritable mechanisms of resistance to pexiganan, an analogue of magainin, when propagated in medium supplemented with this antimicrobial peptide for 600-700 generations.

facts.claim: Emerging contaminants such as endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs), persistent organic pollutants (POPs), and microplastics also significantly influence the emergence, evolution, and dissemination of bacterial antimicrobial resistance.
facts.quote: In addition to antibiotics themselves, emerging contaminants such as endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs), persistent organic pollutants (POPs), and microplastics also significantly influence the emergence, evolution, and dissemination of bacterial antimicrobial resistance.

facts.claim: Antibiotic selection can drive the evolution of duplicated antibiotic resistance genes through MGE transposition.
facts.quote: Modeling and experiments show that antibiotic selection can drive the evolution of duplicated antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) through MGE transposition.

facts.claim: Duplicated antibiotic resistance genes are highly enriched in bacteria isolated from humans and livestock.
facts.quote: Duplicated ARGs are highly enriched in bacteria isolated from humans and livestock.

facts.claim: The selective pressures caused by increased use and misuse of antimicrobials in medicine and livestock production have accelerated the overall selection of resistant bacteria.
facts.quote: The selective pressures caused by increased use and misuse of antimicrobials in medicine and livestock production have accelerated the overall selection of resistant bacteria.
facts.causalWarning: causal wording, but the cited study only shows an association

research.angle: Antibiotic use and environmental contaminants drive the evolution of resistance through mechanisms like gene duplication, horizontal gene transfer, and independent evolution in specific lineages.
research.verdict: The evidence confirms that antibiotic use and environmental factors accelerate the selection and spread of resistance genes, including the evolution of resistance to novel antimicrobial peptides.
research.caveat: While many mechanisms are identified, there is an urgent need to further investigate the specific mechanisms of antimicrobial-induced horizontal transfer.
